bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for EV and export capacity; no dividend payout in Q2FY22; plan to resume dividends in FY23 if cash flow improves; no M&A planned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material volatility (steel/aluminum); global supply chain disruptions; currency fluctuations (60% revenue in USD/EUR); delayed EV adoption in India
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; emphasized execution on pricing and cost control; confident on export demand and EV pipeline; acknowledged inflation headwinds but highlighted pricing power with Tier-1 OEMs
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Wheels India is one of the few Indian suppliers with certified EV wheel platforms for European OEMs — a niche advantage not widely recognized by investors
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Steel wheels: 65% revenue; Alloy wheels: 30% revenue (growth at 25% YoY); Aftermarket: 5% revenue; EV wheels: ₹320cr orderbook, 15% of total orderbook

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin at 11.8% in Q2FY22 (down 120 bps YoY due to steel/aluminum inflation); pricing actions implemented in Q3FY22 to recover 80 bps; cost optimization through automation reducing labor cost by 15%
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth of 15-20% FY22E; EBITDA margin to stabilize at 12-13% in H2FY22; capex of ₹250cr for FY22 focused on EV and export capacity.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹1,850cr (60% from exports; 40% domestic; EV segment orderbook: ₹320cr)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion in Thailand and Mexico plants to serve global OEMs; entry into two new EV platforms in FY22; potential entry into carbon fiber wheel R&D with partner
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Wheels India is a leading domestic supplier of steel and alloy wheels with strong export exposure and growing EV wheel volumes, positioned to benefit from India's auto export boom and OEM electrification. Margins are under pressure from raw material inflation but improving with pricing actions and operational efficiency.
